_doc: Ground colours for panels (style bible §3). A panel's "ground" is one of these names, or a hex. A panel's "sky" (above the horizon) takes the same names. A colour is a hex; [top, bottom], a vertical gradient (night); or { "horizontal": [left, right] } (sky-blue). Every ground carries a gradient, the direction picked arbitrarily (2026-11-11), to be reviewed; the first colour is the original flat one. Artist's rule (2026-11-08): backgrounds are light — off-white (light beige), light-grey, even white; greens only for top views (03.01) and the land strip under a sky/horizon (05.12); dusty-pink never. 2026-11-15: sage and forest dropped (too close to dry-grass and dark-green), green added (a brighter green). night-blue: a more saturated night (chapter 10). TRIAL (2026-11-25, branch summer-grounds): every colour is its nearest swatch of the artist's 12-colour palette (off-white, light-grey, white, sand, stone-grey: sand; dry-grass: grass and mist: blue-sky, the second nearest, so land and sky stay apart from sand), shading to 88% of it (the nights 62%, or a night horizon vanishes) in the direction it had; heat-wave, ocean and lake are the swatches nothing matched.
